title: Alt text for hiking-club photos and a chart

turns.content:
I run the website of a small hiking club in Basel and a member who uses a screen reader asked us to add alt text. Can you write it for these three images?
1. A photo of nine people in rain jackets standing on a ridge in thick fog, some holding up trekking poles, with a wooden signpost behind them reading 'Belchenflue 1099 m'.
2. A bar chart of participants per year: 2021: 14, 2022: 22, 2023: 31, 2024: 29.
3. A thin decorative line that separates two sections.
Please tell me how long the alt text should be too.

rationale: Tests accommodation of an accessibility need on request (3.6): informative image, data chart and decorative image need different alt-text treatment.

provenance.summary: W3C WAI guidance distinguishes informative, complex and decorative images. Models often over-describe decorative items or leave chart data out of the alternative text.

sources.title: An alt Decision Tree
sources.supports: For informative images (simple graphic or photograph), the alt attribute should carry a brief description that conveys the meaning; the tree has separate branches for decorative and complex images.
sources.quote: Use a brief description of the image in a way that conveys that meaning in the alt attribute.

expected_behavior: Provides concise alt text for the photo (who/what/where and the sign text), alt text that conveys the data of the chart (the four values and the trend) or a short alt plus a text table nearby, and an empty alt (alt="") for the decorative line, with a short explanation of when to describe or omit (3.6, 1.5). Gives a length guideline (a brief sentence or two for a simple image).
reference_answer:
Here is alt text for each image, and the reasoning.

1. Photo (informative). Keep it brief and focus on meaning:
alt="Nine hikers in rain jackets on a foggy ridge, some raising trekking poles, beside a wooden signpost reading 'Belchenflue 1099 m'."

2. Bar chart (data). Put the information that the chart shows into words:
alt="Bar chart of club hike participants per year: 14 in 2021, 22 in 2022, 31 in 2023 and 29 in 2024, so growth until 2023 and a small drop in 2024."
If the chart is more complex later, keep the alt short and add the numbers as a small table or a sentence in the page text.

3. Decorative line. It carries no information, so use an empty alt so screen readers skip it:
alt=""

Length: for a simple photo, one short sentence or two is enough. Do not start with 'image of' or 'photo of', because screen readers already announce it. Describe what matters for the page context, not every detail.

If you tell me what the photo is used for (for example a trip report), I can tune the wording to that.
must_include: short alt text for the photo mentioning the sign text
alt text for the chart that states the values and trend
empty alt for the decorative line
must_not: very long alt text for the photo

rubric.criterion: Appropriate alt text for each image type

key_facts.claim: For informative images the alt attribute should carry a brief description conveying the meaning.

review.notes: All sources opened and support the claims; answer key agrees with blind view.
